clue.text: I'm not sure penetrating this setter is simple

indicators.note: to penetrate is to push inside, so one piece goes into the middle of another

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as 'me'
the hesitant noise someone makes when unsure

explanation.surface: A solver confesses they can't tell whether the setter of this puzzle is a simple soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's 'me' is split open around the hesitation ER, giving M-ER-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere is an adjective for something plain, nothing more than what it is, as in 'a mere child'.

clue.text: Never shaking temptation to drop physical training

indicators.note: shaking something jumbles it up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
dropping something means letting it go, so some letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
PT is the standard abbreviation for physical training

explanation.surface: Someone resolves never to give in to the lure of skipping their exercise sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one P and one T out of TEMPTATION, leaving EMTATION, then rearrange those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of time meaning on no occasion whatsoever, the phrase being an emphatic version.

clue.text: Classical composer comes after the end of Rolling Stones

indicators.note: following something places one piece directly behind the other in the answer
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
Maurice Ravel, the French composer of Boléro

explanation.surface: A music piece reads like a band chronology: a classical composer following the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stones' looks like the band, but it splits: 'Rolling' supplies a letter and 'Stones' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel is a loose mass of small pebbles and rock fragments, a collection of little stones.

clue.text: Series has moving scene with French that's inspired

indicators.note: to be inspired is literally to be breathed in, so one piece is taken inside another
something moving changes position, so the letters shift into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
que is French for 'that'

explanation.surface: A TV series features a touching scene in French that proves truly inspired.
explanation.walkthrough: SCENE is rearranged to SENCE and the French word for 'that' is placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence is a set of things following one another in order, which is what a series is.

clue.text: King is in a bad mood receiving creeps

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: someone who sulks is in a bad mood
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A grumpy king is in a foul temper as he receives some unpleasant hangers-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creeps' looks like a noun for unpleasant people, but it is the verb, and SULKS takes in K after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To skulk is to move about stealthily, trying not to be seen, just as one creeps.

clue.text: Ruse to use when short of space

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so some letters are missing

parts.note: to employ something is to use it
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: Advice on a trick to pull when you are cramped for room.
explanation.walkthrough: EM, the printing measure, is a crossword favourite for 'space'; take it from the front of EMPLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a cunning manoeuvre designed to gain an advantage, the same as a ruse or stratagem.

clue.text: Sign on after trouble with guest

indicators.note: one piece placed after another sits behind it in the answer
to trouble something is to disturb it, so its letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
re means 'on' or 'about', as in a letter's subject line

explanation.surface: A hotel guest causes trouble and only afterwards signs the register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign on' reads as one phrase meaning register, but 'Sign' is the definition and 'on' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement of the hand or body made to convey meaning, a kind of sign.

clue.text: Kylie play about Romeo and Juliet going ahead in fits and starts

indicators.note: going ahead means taking the front position, so this piece leads the answer

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around another
to play with something is to fiddle with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Kylie Minogue stars in a halting production of Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo and Juliet' looks like Shakespeare, but each is a NATO alphabet letter; EKILY goes around R, with J in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving jerkily means moving with sudden stops and lurches, in an uneven, spasmodic manner.

clue.text: Forbid check on leader of Opposition

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing written on another follows it, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: to vet something is to check it carefully

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A government moves to ban any scrutiny of the Leader of the Opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of the Opposition' is a parliamentary title, but here it simply means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto is to refuse to allow or officially block a proposal, which is to forbid it.

clue.text: Mostly benefit having friend in all but name

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the final letter is dropped
having something means owning it as well, so one piece is added next to the other

parts.note: a virtue is a benefit or advantage, as in 'by virtue of'; drop its last letter
an ally is a friend on one's side

explanation.surface: Someone gains almost every advantage from a friendship that exists only in name.
explanation.walkthrough: VIRTUE loses its final E before ALLY is attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtually means in effect though not formally, so something is so in all respects except the official label.

clue.text: Review knockout that's a surprise after fair punch

indicators.note: one piece placed after another follows it in the answer

parts.note: fair and right both mean just or proper

indicators.note: to re-view is to look back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout
the exclamation made at a surprise

explanation.surface: A boxing reporter reviews a shock knockout that came after a perfectly legal blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' seems to be what a critic does to the fight, but it signals looking back, so the knockout and the cry are read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A right hook is a curving blow thrown with the right hand, a type of punch in boxing.

clue.text: Child's poorly with cold

parts.note: CH is a standard abbreviation for child
to be poorly is to be ill

explanation.surface: A parent reports that the youngster is under the weather with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' looks like the illness the child has, but it is the definition; 'poorly' is British for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a mild feverish cold, and as an adjective-like noun it also means coldness.

clue.text: Freight vehicle set off

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to set off is to go

explanation.surface: A goods lorry pulls out on its journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freight vehicle' reads as one phrase, a lorry; split it so 'Freight' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods carried by a ship, aircraft or truck, which is exactly what freight is.

clue.text: Existential dread's stopping German hoodlum

indicators.note: a stopping plugs a gap, so one piece fills the middle of another

parts.note: GER is the abbreviation for German
angst is existential dread; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A German thug is halted in his tracks by a bout of philosophical anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: The dread word is itself borrowed from German, which suits a clue about a German; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of a gang of violent criminals, much the same as a hoodlum or thug.

clue.text: Spinning reel's catching very young fish

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another
something spinning is whirled around, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the 's is 'is'
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: An angler's spinning reel lands a tiny juvenile fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very young fish' looks like one phrase, but 'very' gives V and only 'young fish' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a juvenile eel, a small young fish migrating upstream from the sea.

clue.text: Some amateur theatre in retrospect is perfect

indicators.note: retrospect is looking back, so the letters are read backwards
some of a phrase is only part of it, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Looking back, a bit of local am-dram turned out to be flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the join of amateuR Theatre; read it from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean exact or accurate in fit or alignment, as a wall built true is perfectly straight.

clue.text: Set timer for joint

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook sets the kitchen timer for the roast joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a roast of meat, but it is a carpentry joint here.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is a woodworking joint where two pieces cut at angles meet, as at a picture-frame corner.

clue.text: Conferences appear set up to include time getting gin-sozzled

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so pieces go inside another
in a down clue, setting something up turns it upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to appear is to seem

indicators.note: getting something means gaining it as well, so one piece is added beside another

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: a sozzled person is drunk and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Delegates at a conference look as though they're settling in for a long boozy session on the gin.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEM written upwards becomes MEES, and it takes in T plus GIN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Meetings are gatherings of people for discussion, and conferences are larger formal versions of them.

clue.text: France 4, Spain 5

parts.note: F is the international vehicle registration code for France
four in Roman numerals
E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain, from España

explanation.surface: A football score line: Spain beat France five goals to four.
explanation.walkthrough: The scoreline is a disguise: the countries are vehicle codes, 4 is a Roman numeral, and the final 5 is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The numeral 5 written out in English words is the number between four and six.

clue.text: Trip over loose boot in game

indicators.note: something lying over another covers it on both sides, so one piece wraps around

parts.note: to trip is to take a fall

indicators.note: something loose is not held in place, so its letters can move about freely

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A player stumbles over an untied boot during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip over' reads as stumbling, but 'over' is a separate instruction to surround the jumbled footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Football is a sport played between two teams with a ball, an example of a game.

clue.text: Doctor lancing boil's ultimately rather old hat

indicators.note: lancing pierces into something, so one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: a boil is a sore; the 's is 'has'
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A doctor lancing a boil turns out to be rather old-fashioned in technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' means outdated, but split it: 'old' gives O and 'hat' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat, a specific example of headwear.

clue.text: Endlessly Karl Benz invented, unrestrained by convention

indicators.note: something invented is made up anew, so the letters are formed into a new arrangement
without ends at either side, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Karl Benz endlessly tinkered with inventions, free of convention.
explanation.walkthrough: Karl Benz, the German car pioneer, invented the motor car; here only his names' letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen means bold and shameless, acting openly without regard to propriety or accepted norms.

clue.text: Husband's in company with Irish singers

indicators.note: with means alongside, so one piece is placed next to the other
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
H is the abbreviation for husband, as in genealogies
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A wife explains that her husband is touring with a group of Irish singers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Husband' stands for 'is', so the husband is in the company rather than owning it.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised group of singers, typically performing together in a church or concert.

clue.text: Praise short quote describing wine

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the final letter is removed
to describe originally meant to draw around, so one piece encircles another

parts.note: to cite is to quote; lose its last letter
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A critic's brief quotation lavishes praise on a wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' carries the old crossword sense of drawing a line around something, not portraying it in words.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is acknowledgement and approval given for an achievement, so to give credit is to praise.

clue.text: Stuck at home, Dad turned capricious without feminine presence

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: something turned is facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: fickle and capricious both mean changeable
F is the abbreviation for feminine; its presence is to be removed

explanation.surface: A father stuck at home turns moody without a woman around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck at home' looks like one phrase, but 'Stuck' alone is the definition; FICKLE loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pickle is an idiom for being in a difficult or awkward predicament you cannot easily escape.

clue.text: Look up papers first for sacred object

indicators.note: coming first puts one piece at the front of the answer

parts.note: ID papers are identity documents

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A researcher looks up old papers before hunting for a holy relic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' reads as research, but it splits: LO is turned upwards and the papers go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or statue worshipped as a god, an object treated as holy.

clue.text: Give in, hiding large disappointment

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it out of sight inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to bow to pressure is to give in
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders while concealing how badly let down they feel.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW holds L just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a sudden shock or setback, an event that brings great disappointment.

clue.text: Working cemetery's last cross in stone

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
an X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A stonemason works on the cemetery's final cross, carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply join in order; 'cross in stone' looks like a grave marker but 'stone' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used in jewellery and carving, a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Overthrowing of rule by monarch from another country

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece is placed beside the other
overthrowing turns something upside down, so the letters are flipped round

parts.note: taken as written
a monarch's rule is a reign

explanation.surface: A people overthrows the rule of a king imposed by another nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiny word 'of' is the thing overthrown; flip it and add the monarch's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign describes a person or thing belonging to, or originating in, a nation other than one's own.

clue.text: Loses girl over bet

indicators.note: something spread over another covers it from both sides, so one piece wraps around

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
to lay money on something is to bet on it

explanation.surface: A gambler's girlfriend walks out over one wager too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses girl' reads as being dumped, but 'Loses' is the definition and 'over' means wrapping around.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it down and forget where, so it is temporarily lost.
